reason: The current contextual ItemAttention model scores 0.370 macro validation HR@10 versus SASRec's 0.505, with declines in every category; separate history and target embeddings are a plausible contributor, not an established cause. Successful historical models used tied embeddings, while adding contextualization alone failed to recover performance, supporting the initial plan's controlled embedding-sharing experiment. Modify model_design for parameter sharing and training_evaluation for matching checkpoint reconstruction, leaving data processing and the training protocol fixed.

Initialize this shared table exactly once with the existing normal standard deviation 0.05 and zero padding row; retain model.parameters() so AdamW receives each shared parameter only once. Sharing lets history-side and candidate-side supervision update the same item representations and approximately halves item-embedding parameters, testing the initial hypothesis without adopting historical architecture or objective changes. Preserve ItemAttention constructor arguments, forward(self, seq, candidates), predict(self, seq, candidates), dimension 96, two contextual blocks, two heads, dropout 0.2, positional embeddings, history_key, target_query, normalization, candidate-conditioned pooling, learned scales, recency decay, item_bias, and the scoring formula. Keep the sampled-softmax loss and existing two-term embedding-penalty formula unchanged, evaluating both terms through the shared table without changing their coefficient, AdamW settings, or gradient clipping.
